::: {#thm-mse-rss}
#### Mean squared error is the residual sum of squares divided by $n$

For a regression model with conditional mean $\mean(x; \vparam)$,
the [mean squared error](estimation.qmd#def-prediction-mse)
of its predictions $\fitted_i = \mean(x_i; \vparam)$
of $n \ge 1$ outcomes $\dsn{y}$
and the residual sum of squares $\text{RSS}(\vparam)$ (@def-rss)
over those same $n$ outcomes satisfy

$$\mselr{\fitted} = \frac{1}{n} \text{RSS}(\vparam),$$

and equivalently

$$\text{RSS}(\vparam) = n \, \mselr{\fitted}.$$
:::

::: proof
Both equations are derived in @exr-mse-rss.
:::

::: {#rem-mse-rss}
#### The same observations on both sides

The identities in @thm-mse-rss need the mean squared error
and the residual sum of squares to be taken over the same $n$ observations.
The RSS minimized in fitting is taken over the fitting data,
so dividing it by $n$ gives the mean squared error on the fitting data,
not the mean squared error of predictions of new outcomes.
:::
